::: {.research-intro}
My research uses household survey and panel data from Ethiopia to study how smallholder farmers produce and sell, and how households cope when shocks hit. Most of it is applied microeconometrics: stochastic frontier models, instrumental variables and panel data methods.

[ORCID profile](https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5588-2301){.btn .btn-outline-navy} [View CV](cv.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-navy}
:::

## Interests {.research-h2}

::: {.card-grid .card-grid-3 .research-interests}
::: {.card-soft .interest}
[[]{.bi .bi-flower1}]{.interest-icon}

### Smallholder productivity

Technical efficiency and input adoption on Ethiopian farms, measured with stochastic frontier models.
:::

::: {.card-soft .interest}
[[]{.bi .bi-shop}]{.interest-icon}

### Crop commercialization

Whether farmers who sell more of their cereal harvest are more efficient. My Ghent thesis used instrumental variables to answer it, and I am reworking it into a paper on productivity misallocation.
:::

::: {.card-soft .interest}
[[]{.bi .bi-basket}]{.interest-icon}

### Food insecurity and shocks

How exposed urban and rural households are when a shock hits the whole economy, and whether the urban advantage in food security holds up.
:::
:::
